title: The Parts of a Plate
bigQuestion: What goes on a plate to make a good lunch?

story.title: The Paper Plate Lunch
story.kicker: The class builds a lunch out of colored paper, and the plate tells a story.
paragraphs: Ms. Ortiz put a big paper plate on each table. Next to it was a pile of paper food. Red apples. Green broccoli. Brown bread. A yellow cheese slice. A pink piece of fish.
"Build a lunch," she said. Leo grabbed three pieces of bread and a cookie. Ana picked an apple, some carrots, rice and a chicken leg. She put a paper cup of milk on the side.
Ms. Ortiz walked by. She looked at Leo's plate. "What colors do you see?" Leo looked. "Brown. Just brown." He looked at Ana's plate. Red, orange, white and tan. "Hers looks like a rainbow."
Leo traded one bread for an apple. He traded the cookie for a slice of cheese. Now his plate had four colors. "That is a plate with parts," said Ms. Ortiz. "Every part has a job."
story.think: What did Leo change on his plate, and why do you think it helped?

lessons.title: Fruits and Vegetables
lessons.mainIdea: Fruits and vegetables come from plants and should fill half your plate.
reading: Look at an apple. Look at a carrot. Both grew on a plant. The apple is a *fruit*. The carrot is a *vegetable*. They are two food groups.
Fruits are often sweet. Apples, bananas, grapes and oranges are fruits. Vegetables are things like carrots, broccoli, corn and peas.
Here is the rule. Make half your plate fruits and vegetables. Picture a plate. Draw a line down the middle. One side is plants.

words.d: a sweet food that grows on a plant, like an apple or a grape
a plant food like a carrot, broccoli or peas

look.title: Half a Plate
look.text: Look at a round plate. A line goes down the middle. On the left side there are grapes and green beans. On the right side there is a roll and a piece of chicken. The left side is full. The right side is full too.
look.prompt: Which side of the plate is the fruits and vegetables? Is it half?

check.why: A banana is sweet and grows on a plant. It is a fruit.

check.q: How much of your plate should be fruits and vegetables?
check.why: The rule is half your plate. That is a lot of plants.
Broccoli is a plant food that is not sweet. It is a vegetable.

lessons.title: Grains, Protein and Dairy
lessons.mainIdea: Grains, protein foods and dairy are the other three groups on your plate.
reading: Bread, rice, noodles and cereal are *grains*. Grains come from plants like wheat and rice. They give you energy to run and play.
Chicken, fish, beans, eggs and nuts are *protein* foods. Protein helps your body grow. Milk, cheese and yogurt are *dairy*. Dairy helps your bones.
Count the groups. Fruits. Vegetables. Grains. Protein. Dairy. That is five. A good plate has a little of each one.

words.d: foods like bread, rice and cereal that come from wheat or rice plants
foods like chicken, beans and eggs that help you grow
foods made from milk, like cheese and yogurt

look.title: Sort the Lunch
look.text: Look at a lunch tray. There is a slice of pizza with cheese on top. There is a cup of peaches. There is a carton of milk. There are baby carrots. There is a hard-boiled egg.
look.prompt: Name the group for each food. Which food might fit two groups?

check.why: Rice comes from a rice plant. It is a grain like bread.
Cheese is made from milk. Milk foods are dairy.

check.q: How many food groups are there?
check.why: Fruits, vegetables, grains, protein and dairy make five groups.

lessons.title: Eat a Rainbow
lessons.mainIdea: Different colors of fruits and vegetables help your body in different ways.
reading: Look at a bowl of fruit. Red strawberries. Orange oranges. Yellow bananas. Green grapes. Purple plums. That is a *rainbow* of food.
Each color helps your body a different way. Orange foods help your eyes. Green foods help you grow. So eat many colors, not just one.
Try this at lunch. Count the colors on your plate. One color? Add a fruit. Two colors? Add a vegetable. More colors is better.

words.d: many colors together; a plate with red, green, orange and more

look.title: Colors on Two Plates
look.cite: Example plates from the paper plate lunch story
look.prompt: Which plate has the most colors? What could Leo add to get to three?

check.q: What does eat a rainbow mean?
choices: Eat fruits and vegetables of many colors
check.why: A rainbow of plants means many colors. Each color helps in its own way.

check.q: Your plate has only brown foods. What can you add?
check.why: A fruit or a vegetable adds a new color to the plate.
Orange foods like carrots help your eyes see well.

lessons.title: Water Every Day
lessons.mainIdea: Water is the everyday drink; it keeps your body working and costs nothing.
reading: You ran at recess. Your face is hot. Your mouth is dry. Your body is asking for *water*. Go to the fountain and drink.
Water is the everyday drink. It has no sugar. It keeps you cool. Milk is a good drink too. It is dairy.
Juice and soda are sweet. They are sometimes drinks. Water is for every day. Keep a water bottle at your desk.

words.d: the everyday drink; it has no sugar and keeps your body cool

look.title: After Recess
look.text: Look at three cups on a table. One has water. One has milk. One has soda. Two kids just ran in from recess. They are hot and thirsty. Each kid gets to pick one cup.
look.prompt: Which cup is the everyday drink? Which one is a sometimes drink?

check.q: Which drink is the everyday drink?
check.why: Water has no sugar and cools your body. It is for every day.

check.q: You are hot after playing. What should you drink first?
check.why: Water cools you and fills up what you lost from sweating.
Milk comes from the dairy group. It helps your bones.

sections.title: New Foods and Where Food Comes From

lessons.title: Trying a New Food
lessons.mainIdea: It can take many tries to like a new food, so take one small taste each time.
reading: A green pepper slice is on your plate. You never ate one. It looks strange. Do you have to like it? No. Do you have to try it? Just a *taste*.
Here is the plan. Take one small bite. Chew. Think. Then say yes or no thank you. Many kids need ten tries to like a new food.
So try again another day. Your tongue can change its mind. Lots of foods you love now were new once.

words.d: one small bite to find out what a food is like

look.title: The Strange Green Slice
look.text: Look at a lunch plate. There is a sandwich, some grapes, and one slice of green pepper. A boy pokes the pepper with his fork. He has never seen one on his plate before. He makes a face.
look.prompt: What is one small thing the boy could do before he says no?

check.q: A new food is on your plate. What should you do?
check.why: One small taste is the fair way to find out if you like it.

check.q: You tried a food once and did not like it. What next?
choices: Eat a whole plate of it
check.why: It can take many tries to like a new food. Your taste can change.

check.q: About how many tries can it take to like a new food?
check.why: Many kids need ten or more tries. Keep tasting.

lessons.title: Farm, Garden, Store
lessons.mainIdea: Food comes from farms and gardens before it gets to the store and your plate.
reading: Look at the apple in your lunch. Where did it come from? The store? Before that, it grew on a tree. The tree was on a *farm*.
A farm grows lots of food. Corn, wheat, apples, beans. Farms also raise cows for milk and chickens for eggs. Trucks take the food to the store.
A *garden* is a tiny farm. You can grow a tomato in a pot. Illinois has many farms. Lots of them grow corn and soybeans.

words.d: a big place where people grow food and raise animals
a small place, even a pot, where you grow food

look.title: The Apple's Trip
look.text: Picture four cards in a row. Card one: an apple tree on a farm. Card two: a truck full of apples. Card three: a store shelf. Card four: an apple in a lunch box. Now the cards get mixed up.
look.prompt: Put the cards back in order. What comes first, and what comes last?

choices: On a tree on a farm
check.why: Apples grow on trees. Farms grow them, then stores sell them.

check.q: What comes right after the farm?
check.why: Trucks carry food from farms to stores.

choices: A small place to grow food
check.why: A garden is a small farm. Even a pot can be a garden.

review.q: Which two groups should fill half your plate?
review.why: The rule is half your plate fruits and vegetables.

review.q: Which food is a protein food?
review.why: Eggs, beans, chicken and fish are protein foods.
Those five groups make up a plate.

review.q: Why eat many colors of fruits and vegetables?
choices: Each color helps your body a different way
review.why: Orange helps eyes, green helps you grow. Many colors help many ways.
Water has no sugar and is for every day.

review.q: Where does food come from before the store?
review.why: Food grows on farms and in gardens first.
